headline: A software developer known for free Adobe-style tools has now released free, open-source alternatives to Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint and Word, made with the Claude AI system.
score_reason: Lowered from 6: this continues a story we carried on 9 Oct 2026, it rests on one outlet, and the article itself says most of the apps are still far from the programs they imitate.
importance_line: Anyone who resents paying a subscription for office software could eventually get a free alternative on Windows, macOS and Linux, but Tom's Hardware says most of these apps are still far from the programs they imitate, and critics have dismissed AI-written software of this kind as 'slop'.
summary: Tom's Hardware reports that Brandon Thomas, the developer behind ArtCraft (a free, open-source set of tools modelled on Adobe programs), has released GridCraft, DeckCraft and WordCraft, free alternatives to Microsoft's Excel, PowerPoint and Word that he built with Anthropic's Claude and shared on GitHub. This follows the report in our 9 Oct 2026 edition on a Reddit user known as u/ai_art_is_art and his Adobe-style tools; Tom's Hardware now names him and says most of the apps are still far from what they aim to replace.
notes: Read in full from the main session's fulltext copy. Follow-up of the 9 Oct 2026 edition item 60 (Tom's Hardware, score 6). The date the new apps were released is not stated; Tom's Hardware published on 11 Oct 2026.
